name: Mach-Hommy
notes: The quietest model in this batch, and deliberately so: the research says drums are "frequently none", and where they exist it is "a soft kick on 1 and a whisper-level snare on 2&4, no hats". Whisper is `velocityTiers` at 72–88 / 46–58 / 22–32, below every other entry here including Boldy James, and `kick.syncopation` 0.03 with `densityPerBar` 1–2 is a kick that does one thing. "Almost no engineered low end" is a bassline register of 19–37 with no glide and one passing tone. "Loops unquantised in pitch" and "sometimes with tape wobble" is `quantizeStrength` 0.66 and `velocityVar` 0.22 — looser than the other minimalists, because the wobble is in the source rather than in the placement. "Long silences" is `dropOutBeats` at 0.55 for four beats, and "verses of irregular length" is a `verse` of 8–24 bars against Boldy's 24–32. ⚠ `hihat.continuous` false at `fillDensity` 0.28 is the floor: a declared hat block owes every seed a hat, so a genuinely hatless record is not expressible and this is the nearest legal thing. ⚠ `confidence` is medium and the research marks the artist-specific parameters `[LOW-CONF]` — the drumless idiom is documented, this artist's numbers are not, so every velocity and density above is an inference from the scene rather than from him. ⚠ The `i–VII` and `i–VI` families at weights 2 and 1 are **INFERRED**; the research names static `i` only. ⚠ **The bass pool was widened after `bass.rs` measured it at 0.851 distinct against a floor of 0.95.** It was authored passingTones ["m7"], followRootsProb 0.84, anticipationProb 0.1 over register [19,37] — a faithful description of a sample-loop bass, and one that leaves a seed nothing to vary but root and octave. Now ["P5","m7"], root lock 0.84, anticipation 0.2, register [19,41]. The line is still overwhelmingly root-on-kick; what changed is how many different records it can be, not how busy any one of them is. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [42, 84] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 33 against a bass reaching 41, an overlap of 9. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 771 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
